# Acecore, Supplya and Navidyn are betting Nigeria can build, lend and dive
[![Acecore, Supplya and Navidyn are betting Nigeria can build, lend and dive](https://c76c7bbc41.mjedge.net/wp-content/uploads/tc/2026/11/Acecore.webp)](https://techcabal.com/2026/11/10/acecore-supplya-and-navidyn-moonshot/) _The Acecore team receives the $10,000 cheque for winning TC Battlefield 2026 at Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos._

## **Navidyn**
[Navidyn](https://www.navidynrobotics.com/) built the robot before the company.

Atabot is an observation-class remotely operated vehicle, or ROV, rated to 50 metres with a battery that lasts 36 minutes. Navidyn plans to rent it at $4,000 a day, add lump-sum fees for bigger jobs, and sell machines later. It will start with small and medium-sized offshore operators in shallow water, and wants $800,000 to finish a product, land a first recurring contract, and fund 18 months.

Navidyn’s case rests on a shift in who owns Nigeria’s oil.

Renting by the day puts Navidyn in the same business as operators that already own vessels, crews and imported fleets, and work-class machines handle jobs Atabot cannot yet do.

Navidyn’s list of 50 target companies splits into 23 small, 22 medium and 13 large, which adds up to 58. Ogaji also works as a lead engineer at a Texas-based drone manufacturer. At the pitch, the founders [said](https://techcabal.com/2026/11/03/acecore-wins-tc-battlefield/) that a Sahara Group representative offered a $5,000 inspection job before the product was ready.
